main_body: farm building with a sloped tiled roof and vertical wooden front wall
top_band: red-brown tiled roof slope with ridge cap and front eave trim from row 5 to row 57 (excluding central dormer/chimney)
evidence: The building shows a large foreshortened top/sloped roof surface (rows 5-57) with a clear bright front eave edge at rows 56-57, a dark eave shadow at rows 58-60, and a vertical front wall with doors and windows from row 58 to 93.

style.evidence: While the roof has a 4-5 step tile pattern, the pattern is a rigid, mechanical 3x3 grid repeat lacking the varied highlights and diagonal shading of the Beodeul reference roofs. More importantly, the lower wall is composed of simple 1px vertical stripes and flat 2-3 colour geometric barn doors and windows, which look much flatter, cleaner, and less textured than the richly detailed stone and timber-framed plaster walls and shaded wooden doors in the Beodeul references. Furthermore, the dormer roof (rows 27-37) is drawn as a flat front-facing triangle with no visible top slopes, unlike the reference gable.
